l4_steps.name: Pull daily crew duty roster from CMS
l4_steps.input: Published monthly roster, intraday amendments, real-time crew updates
l4_steps.output: Day-of-operations crew duty list with flight assignments and report times
l4_steps.kpi: Roster accuracy ≥99% match to published pairings; list generated ≥3 hrs before first departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Late roster amendments from crew bidding workflow can cause data sync lag between Jeppesen and Altéa PSS, risking crew data mismatches at check-in during hub-complex rotations

l4_steps.name: Send automated duty-start notifications to crew
l4_steps.input: Day-of-operations crew duty list, crew contact and mobile app registration database
l4_steps.output: SMS and app push notifications with report time, flight number, aircraft registration, and gate
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥99.5% within 30 min of duty window opening; read-receipt confirmed for ≥90% of app-registered crew
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew mobile app adoption varies across base seniority groups; SMS fallback provides no read-receipt confirmation, creating unverified notification risk for critical duty changes during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Verify crew check-in at required report time
l4_steps.input: Crew self-reported check-in entries, kiosk or app check-in timestamps, scheduled report times
l4_steps.output: Confirmed check-in log; no-show flag with timestamp for absent crew members
l4_steps.kpi: On-time check-in rate ≥98%; no-show detection and standby activation trigger within 15 min of missed report time
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual check-in verification at outstations with no dedicated crew desk compresses the standby activation window; regional airport staffing gaps mean no-shows may not be detected until gate agents escalate, often inside 60 min to departure

l4_steps.name: Validate crew qualifications, recency & type currency
l4_steps.input: Crew training records from LMS integration, qualification and recency database, aircraft type assignment
l4_steps.output: Qualification check pass/fail decision; restriction flags forwarded to pairing optimizer
l4_steps.kpi: Zero qualified-crew-on-illegal-assignment incidents; automated compliance check runtime ≤2 min per crew member
l4_steps.pain_point: Training record sync delays between the airline LMS and Jeppesen can allow stale qualification data to persist, creating regulatory exposure under FAR Part 61 if a crew member's type rating lapse is not reflected in the CMS before duty commencement

l4_steps.name: Initialize duty period clock & FRMS baseline
l4_steps.input: Confirmed check-in timestamp, crew fatigue risk profile, prior-duty rest duration
l4_steps.output: Active duty record with ACTT (Applicable Cumulative Trip Time) counter initialized; FRMS alerting thresholds set
l4_steps.kpi: Duty record initialization within 5 min of check-in confirmation; FRMS baseline computed for 100% of active crew
l4_steps.pain_point: FRMS models calibrated on aggregate fleet data may underestimate fatigue for crew transitioning from high-density transcontinental rotations into back-to-back short-haul turns, particularly where rest was taken across multiple time zones

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time duty time against FAR Part 117 limits
l4_steps.input: ACARS flight departure and arrival timestamps, active duty records, FAR Part 117 FDP and rest parameters
l4_steps.output: Running duty time totals per crew member; automated alerts triggered at 90% of applicable limit thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAR Part 117 FDP exceedances; alert triggered ≥60 min before any limit breach; alert-to-action response time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS timestamp delays at congested hub airports (e.g., ORD, ATL) can cause duty time calculations to lag actual operations by 5–12 min, compressing the crew controller's response window before a legally binding FDP limit is reached

l4_steps.name: Calculate projected rest requirement & next availability
l4_steps.input: Projected duty end time, FAR Part 117 minimum rest table, hotel inventory data from accommodation vendor API
l4_steps.output: Minimum rest end timestamp; crew availability window for next assignment; hotel block release notification
l4_steps.kpi: Rest calculation accuracy ±0 min (regulatory requirement); hotel release notification issued within 30 min of projected rest start; ≥95% of rest-period hotel blocks confirmed before duty release
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel inventory management for irregular operations is handled outside the CMS via a separate vendor portal, requiring manual coordination that increases the risk of accommodation errors and delays crew rest commencement, eroding the legally mandated minimum rest period

l4_steps.name: Track crew-to-aircraft assignment via ACARS OOOI data
l4_steps.input: Aircraft OOOI (Out/Off/On/In) movement messages, crew assignment records from Jeppesen CMS
l4_steps.output: Real-time crew-aircraft match or mismatch status per flight sector
l4_steps.kpi: Crew position update latency ≤5 min after OOOI event; position mistrack rate <0.5% of daily operated sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS message dropouts in remote or oceanic airspace create position gaps; fallback to manual satellite phone verification adds 15–20 min lag, which is operationally critical for connecting crew or minimum-rest rotations at outstation overnight bases

l4_steps.name: Confirm crew on-board status against PSS manifest
l4_steps.input: Boarding pass scan data, crew manifest from CMS-to-PSS integration feed
l4_steps.output: Confirmed crew on-board record per flight; late-boarding or missing-crew flag escalated to crew desk
l4_steps.kpi: Crew boarding confirmation ≥15 min before STD; zero departures with unresolved unconfirmed crew status
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa crew manifest data refresh depends on the Jeppesen–Altéa integration batch cycle; if the interface runs on a 10-min cadence, last-minute crew swaps may not be reflected in the PSS boarding system, triggering false missing-crew alerts and unnecessary departure holds

l4_steps.name: Update crew position records after each completed sector
l4_steps.input: OOOI timestamps from ACARS, gate arrival confirmation, crew pairing sequence
l4_steps.output: Updated crew position records with current station; next-sector readiness status flag
l4_steps.kpi: Position record updated within 10 min of IN event; data accuracy ≥99.8% match to ACARS source timestamps
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-leg rotations with short turn times under 45 min risk position record overwrites if the prior segment's IN event message arrives after the subsequent segment's OUT event has already been logged, creating a phantom dual-assignment state in the CMS

l4_steps.name: Receive & triage crew-impacting disruption alerts from NOC
l4_steps.input: Flight delay and cancellation alerts from NOC disruption board, ATC ground stop and GDP notifications
l4_steps.output: Crew impact assessment listing affected pairings, downstream connections, and estimated delay propagation
l4_steps.kpi: Initial crew impact assessment within 10 min of disruption notification; zero unacknowledged disruption alerts aged >15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: NOC disruption data feeds into the CMS via a polling API; 5-min polling intervals can delay crew controller awareness of fast-moving ATC programs or ground stops at high-traffic hubs, shortening the window available to proactively cover downstream crew illegalities

l4_steps.name: Assess revised schedule legality for impacted crew
l4_steps.input: Revised flight schedule from operations control, active crew duty records, FAR Part 117 FDP and rest parameters
l4_steps.output: Legal or illegal status for each impacted crew member under revised schedule; extension waiver eligibility flags
l4_steps.kpi: Legality check completed within 15 min of disruption triage; waiver utilization rate <5% of disrupted operations; zero post-event FAR Part 117 violations
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen's automated solver engine may time out on complex network disruptions affecting 20 or more crew simultaneously, requiring manual controller override and extending resolution time beyond the OTP recovery window, particularly during hub-wide weather events

l4_steps.name: Source and assign replacement or standby crew
l4_steps.input: Standby crew availability list, deadhead crew pool, hotel and accommodation records, airport reserve pool by base
l4_steps.output: Confirmed crew reassignment with pairing details; standby activation record; deadhead authorization if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Standby crew activated within 30 min of need identification; deadhead crew positioned within 2 hrs; crew coverage rate ≥97% of disrupted flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Standby pool sizing is optimized for statistically expected disruption levels; severe weather events causing hub ground stops exceeding 4 hrs exhaust local standby pools, forcing cross-base deadhead that itself consumes FAR Part 117 FDP, further compressing available duty time for replacement crews

l4_steps.name: Issue crew reassignment notifications & sync downstream systems
l4_steps.input: Confirmed reassignment records from Jeppesen CMS
l4_steps.output: Push notifications delivered to affected crew; updated pairings in CMS; Altéa PSS crew manifest refreshed; payroll audit trail updated
l4_steps.kpi: Crew notification sent within 5 min of reassignment confirmation; CMS-to-PSS sync completed before gate opens (≥30 min before STD); notification delivery confirmation rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cascading reassignments in multi-hub disruptions generate notification storms; crew mobile app rate limits and carrier network congestion at hub airports cause delivery delays precisely during peak disruption windows when accurate crew information is most critical

l4_steps.name: Confirm crew sign-off & record actual duty-out time
l4_steps.input: Crew self-reported duty-out via mobile app or kiosk, gate departure records, hotel check-in confirmation where applicable
l4_steps.output: Closed duty record with actual block-out to duty-release timestamps; open duty record flag for anomalies
l4_steps.kpi: Duty record closed within 1 hr of crew release; sign-off discrepancy rate <1% of operated duties; open duty record resolution within 4 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Overnight outstations with no crew desk rely entirely on self-reported sign-off via mobile app; connectivity issues at regional airports cause delayed uploads, creating open duty records that block the next crew scheduling build cycle and may delay payroll processing

l4_steps.name: Recalculate 28-day cumulative flight & duty hours
l4_steps.input: Closed duty records, FAR Part 117 cumulative limits (100 hrs per 672-hr window, 1,000 hrs per calendar year), crew fatigue history
l4_steps.output: Updated 28-day and 365-day flight and duty time totals per crew member; scheduling availability flags for next build cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Fatigue record updated within 2 hrs of duty close; zero crew members scheduled before 28-day rolling total validated; cumulative total accuracy ±0 min
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 rolling window calculations across international timezone boundaries introduce date-ambiguity edge cases in legacy CMS implementations, historically requiring manual audit for transmeridian crew rotations and generating compliance review backlog during peak international operation periods

l4_steps.name: Archive duty records & sync actuals to scheduling and payroll
l4_steps.input: Validated duty records with actual block times, fatigue recalculation output
l4_steps.output: Archived duty data package; payroll hours feed to SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO); scheduling feedback to crew pairing optimizer for next build cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll data handoff to SAP within 24 hrs of duty close; scheduling feedback loop complete before next crew build cycle (T+48 hrs); archive integrity check ≥99.99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancies between Jeppesen actual block hours and SAP payroll-recognized hours require manual reconciliation by crew admin; during irregular operations months, reconciliation volume can exceed crew administration capacity, delaying accurate payroll for 2–5% of crew members and generating grievance risk under collective bargaining agreements
